chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from whom he mentioned from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man acquires wealth that is not lawful (haram), then he performs Hajj and says 'Labbayk' (I am here), he is called out: 'Not your 'Labbayk' nor your 'Saadayk' (goodness/joy). And if it is from lawful sources, and he says 'Labbayk', he is called out: 'Your 'Labbayk' and your 'Saadayk'.'
ai.seo_question: Does the source of wealth affect the acceptance of Hajj in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the spiritual efficacy of the Hajj call (*Labbaik*) directly to the purity of the pilgrim's wealth. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that while the ritual acts may be performed, their acceptance (*qabul*) is contingent upon the halal nature of the means used, reflecting the principle that physical devotion is incomplete without financial integrity.
